title: Prove a TPTP problem with Vampire
when: a goal with a first-order encoding (algebra, equational laws, orders) that the Lean battery did not close
finding which premises a proof needs, to hand to grind, aesop or hammer
whenNot: proving the theorem: a Theorem answer is evidence that Lean has not checked (a variable-naming subtlety of Prover9 once gave a wrong announcement in the Equational Theories Project)
higher-order or dependently typed goals: the translation loses them

tptp.description: A TPTP problem (tff or fof) with a conjecture; the axioms' names come back in `used`

timeoutSec.description: Vampire's time limit in seconds, 30 when not given

szs.description: The SZS status line's status (Theorem, CounterSatisfiable, Timeout, GaveUp...), or none

result.description: From the SZS status and the exit code, never from the prose; a Theorem with a nonzero exit code is an error

used.description: The axioms the proof uses, from its file(...) annotations

implementations.description: Vampire as a process (`vampire --input_syntax tptp --proof tptp -t N`, the problem on standard input). The command is a setting (VAMPIRE_COMMAND). Not run: no Vampire binary where this was written.
